title: Compute coupling coefficients
action: Using the given geometry, material indices, effective indices, and wavelength, compute all coupling coefficients (zeta, kappa, iota, varsigma, varpi) from the analytical closed-form expressions derived in the paper. Save the coefficients as an intermediate JSON file for subsequent steps.
description: Intermediate computation of coupling coefficients needed for grating period and insertion loss calculations.
output_schema: A JSON object containing numerical values of the coefficients (zeta_m_nu, kappa_m_nu, iota_nu, varsigma_m, varpi_m), organized by mode index m and harmonic order nu.

title: Compute grating period
action: Compute the grating period Lambda that satisfies the phase-matching conditions for the BMDM design, using the coupling coefficients and the design parameters (ell1=0, ell2=1). Additionally compute the global minimum period Lambda_min. Write the value of Lambda (in nm) to the output file.
description: The grating period in nanometers. The checker will recompute Lambda from the same public parameters and compare the reported value within an absolute tolerance.
output_schema: A single floating-point number representing Lambda in nanometers, with at least two decimal places.

title: Compute insertion losses
action: Using the coupling coefficients and a coupling length L = 34 * Lambda_min, compute the insertion losses IL1 (for first-order mode, codirectional) and IL2 (for second-order mode, contradirectional) under phase-matching (Delta beta = 0). Write the two values (in dB) to the output CSV file.
description: Insertion losses in dB for the two modes. The checker will independently recompute IL1 and IL2 from the same formulas and parameters, and compare the reported values within tolerance.
output_schema: CSV file with header: IL1_dB,IL2_dB. Each row contains two floating-point numbers with at least two decimal places.
